# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *The Old Man and the Sea* that had circulated through the Kettle Harbor Public Library forty-three times since 1998. Marion Reyes found it while checking the book back in: a pencilled note in the margin beside the famous line about the sea, in small, careful handwriting.

*He says "la mar" because he loves her — the Spanish matters. See p. 29 of the original.*

Marion frowned. Page 29 said nothing of the sort. She checked. The note was wrong, or at least wrong in its citation, though the sentiment about the Spanish was accurate. She erased it, or tried to. The pencil had pressed hard enough to emboss the paper. She could still read the ghost of it, like a footprint in wet sand.

She should have reported it. Damaged materials, patron misconduct, a note in the file. Instead she reshelved the book and said nothing, and felt a small, private thrill she couldn't quite explain.

The second note came three weeks later, in a biography of Rachel Carson. *She wrote this chapter while her mother was dying. The sentences are shorter here. Grief edits us.* This one Marion
